thread.title: Trade-war fears are back — but there’s no ‘white-knuckle feeling’ among investors - MarketWatch

author: Victor Reklaitis
title: Trade-war fears are back — but there’s no ‘white-knuckle feeling’ among investors - MarketWatch
text:
Get ready for more chatter about a potential global trade war, thanks to the Trump administration confirming that it may double down on its proposed tariffs on China.
“What was at first a trade skirmish,” writes economist Joseph Stiglitz , “appears to be quickly morphing into a full-scale trade war.”
There already has been “a major uptick in tariff conversation” in second-quarter earnings conference calls, note Bespoke Investment Group’s analysts.
But they’re also highlighting bullish action by key U.S. market measures of risk, as they serve up our call of the day .
The VIX VIX, +9.73% — often called the market’s “fear gauge” — hasn’t climbed much so far, Bespoke’s team points out, saying “that hardly signals a white-knuckle feeling on the part of investors.”
What’s more, junk bonds are still looking good.
“Not only has high yield been relatively unscathed, but the sector has made a new high on a total-return basis over the last few days,” the analysts say, as they share the chart below showing a Merrill Lynch index’s jump above its Jan. 26 peak.
“That’s something we haven’t been able to say since 1/26, which was also the last time the S&P 500 closed at a new high.”

Getting back to their bearish point on trade-related talk, the Bespoke crew says the word “tariff” has already come up 609 different times in the S&P 500’s second-quarter earnings conference calls, up from 290 occurrences in the first quarter. Roughly half of all companies have reported Q2 results so far, the analysts add.

— Bespoke (@bespokeinvest) August 1, 2018 Key market gauges Futures for the Dow YMU8, -0.72% , S&P 500 ESU8, -0.66% and Nasdaq-100 NQU8, -0.77% are losing ground. That’s after the Dow DJIA, -0.32% and S&P SPX, -0.10% closed lower yesterday , while the Nasdaq Composite COMP, +0.46% gained, helped by Apple’s earnings-driven jump.
Trade worries are weighing worldwide: Germany’s DAX DAX, -1.77% is falling nearly 2%, while the Shanghai Composite SHCOMP, -2.00% finished down by 2% .
Oil CLU8, -1.02% and gold GCZ8, -0.30% are falling, as the dollar index DXY, +0.30% gains. Bitcoin BTCUSD, +1.29% is trading around $7,600.
The chart BlackRock drops like a stone as Fidelity goes to zero with its fees. Fidelity Investments announced zero-fee mutual funds yesterday, in a move viewed as a big industry milestone — and also seen as bearish for rivals.
BlackRock’s stock BLK, -4.64% , for example, dived 4.7% in Wednesday’s session, as shown in the chart above. It’s the world’s largest asset manager.
But Fidelity’s free funds aren’t necessarily bad news for Larry Fink & Co., says ISI analyst Glenn Schorr, according to a Dow Jones Newswires report.
BlackRock sells its iShares ETFs commission-free through Fidelity’s brokerage platform, he notes. “Kind of counter-intuitive (and the stock price action doesn’t agree with this), but we believe that if Fidelity is successful in gathering a significant amount of assets with this move, BlackRock could be a beneficiary as well,” Schorr writes.
Read more: Fund fees keep crumbling as investors go cheap and passive
The buzz Tesla’s stock TSLA, +0.91% is 9% higher in premarket action after Elon Musk & Co. posted a wider-than-expected quarterly loss but beat on revenue.
Also helping to assuage recent concerns, Musk sounded more subdued on the conference call, apologizing to analysts and taking a few questions from reporters. He must now get Tesla to achieve his fantastical forecasts, writes MarketWatch’s Therese Poletti .
Reports that Alphabet’s Google GOOG, +0.23% GOOGL, +0.47% could return to China are not true, a state-owned Chinese publication reportedly said , following news that the search king is testing a mobile product that would adhere to Beijing’s strict controls over content.
So proud of Google for developing rich, censor-friendly technology for China. Smart not to let the perfect be the enemy of the good!
— #JeSuisPaulManafortANDmoviepass (@ProfJeffJarviss) August 2, 2018 The companies on the earnings docket ahead of the opening bell include DowDuPont DWDP, -1.18% , Yum YUM, +0.23% , Kellogg K, -2.25% and MGM Resorts MGM, -9.12% .
Weekly jobless claims are due before the open, helping everyone get ready for tomorrow’s monthly jobs report. A release on factory orders is expected once trading is underway.

It’s Super Thursday for the Bank of England , as it releases a rate decision, meeting minutes and an inflation report.
The Vanguard Information Technology ETF VGT, +1.15% managed to avoid some pain from Facebook’s FB, -0.54% stock flop because it has been steadily selling FB shares to prepare for next month’s reclassification of technology stocks.
Reddit has suffered a data breach , but the website has refused to disclose its scale.

The Quote: Getty Images Urban Meyer is on leave. “Forgiving and forgetting domestic violence, sexual assault or abuse against women is no longer the norm. ... It seems Meyer hasn’t changed quickly enough.” — ESPN’s Andrea Adelson is sounding off on the news that Ohio State has put football coach Urban Meyer on paid administrative leave.
OSU’s move follows reports that Meyer may have known of domestic-violence allegations against assistant coach Zach Smith but continued to employ Smith on the Buckeyes’ staff.
